arrears.a:
Instances stop automatically and you get a notification. If the balance stays empty past the published grace period, instances and then data disks are frozen and reclaimed.
The exact windows are shown in Billing; topping up restores the ability to start instances.
arrears.q: What happens when my balance runs out?

billingDisk.a:
By size and calendar day; any part of a day counts as a full day. Resizing settles the current day at the previous size — a larger size is never applied retroactively.
Deleting settles any unbilled days, so a disk created and deleted the same day still costs one day.

billingStart.a:
GPU time is metered per second from the moment the instance reaches Running, and billed hourly. Failed creations cost nothing.
Billing is derived from instance events (see the Events tab); monitoring charts are for display only.

billingStop.a:
Stopping ends GPU charges. What continues is the daily cost: data disks are billed per day (your data stays, so the disk does too).
Release the instance when you no longer need it; data disks are deleted separately.

connectJupyter.a:
The Connect tab link already carries a one-time token — open it directly.
If it says unauthorized, copy the link again from that page (the token can be reset there); resetting invalidates the old link immediately.
Custom images must listen on 0.0.0.0:8888 and read the JUPYTER_TOKEN environment variable, otherwise the entry point will not work.

connectSsh.a:
The instance detail page (Connect tab) shows the full command, like ssh -p <port> root@<host>.
Instances accept key auth only: add your public key under Account settings → SSH keys before creating, and select it at creation time.
If it fails, check the instance is Running, then confirm you are using the matching private key (ssh -i <path>).
connectSsh.q: How do I connect over SSH?

createFailed.a:
If the instance is not ready within 5 minutes it is failed automatically and resources are freed — at no cost. The usual cause is no free GPU for that spec.
Try another tier or model; the Events tab shows the reason.

dataPersist.a:
The instance disk (mounted at /root) survives a stop — your data is still there when you start again. It is wiped only when you release the instance.
A data disk (mounted at /root/data) is independent — releasing the instance keeps it.
Keep your own copies of anything important: after the published grace period on arrears, both instance disks and data disks are reclaimed.
